representative.title: ddPCR for Probes to Target eDNA Samples from Sampled Ecosystems
representative.operation: Probe-based droplet partitioning, endpoint PCR, and droplet fluorescence readout
representative.specimen: Environmental DNA from sampled ecosystems, including water, sediment, biofilm, or soil matrices
representative.platform: Droplet digital PCR; Bio-Rad QX200 or QX600-compatible workflow
representative.methodVariant: Probe-based ddPCR with water-oil emulsion droplet partitioning; supports absolute target quantification and rare-target detection
representative.evidenceStatus: record-metadata-and-license-verified; representative is specific to probe-based droplet dPCR and environmental DNA
representative.selectionNote: Strong, reproducible-looking protocols.io record with stable DOI metadata and a record PDF stating a Creative Commons Attribution License. Selected for its direct fit to absolute quantification and rare-target detection; platform and specimen facets remain explicit because it is not a universal dPCR workflow.

screened.title: Copy Number Variation Analysis by ddPCR
screened.reason: Strong absolute-quantification alternative on a Bio-Rad QX200 droplet platform, but narrower than the selected environmental-DNA rare-target workflow and focused on human copy-number analysis.

screened.title: Digital PCR on the Biomark System
screened.reason: Important microfluidic/IFC partitioning facet on the Biomark platform, but the public record did not provide directly verified reuse-rights evidence for this crawler.

screened.title: Absolute Q Digital PCR System User Guide
screened.reason: Manufacturer microfluidic array-partition workflow is relevant to platform coverage, but the public guide did not expose record-level reuse terms suitable for a reusable representative.

coverageGaps: Non-droplet digital PCR, including microfluidic or array-based partitioning, has no rights-verified representative in this packet.
Clinical blood, tissue, and other non-environmental specimen variants were screened but are not represented by the selected environmental-DNA protocol.
The selected record is probe-based ddPCR; dye-based, multiplex, and platform-specific workflows remain facet-level rather than independently represented.
nextSearchSuggestions: Search protocols.io and Bio-protocol for QuantStudio Absolute Q or Biomark microfluidic digital PCR records with explicit record-level license fields.
Search protocols.io for digital PCR rare-variant detection in blood or clinical tissue with a stable protocol DOI and direct license evidence.
Search Nature Protocols for multiplex dye-based dPCR workflows and compare partitioning method, platform, and specimen facets.

representative.title: PCR Using Q5 Hot Start High-Fidelity DNA Polymerase
representative.operation: High-fidelity thermocycling with Q5 Hot Start polymerase and length-adjusted extension
representative.methodVariant: Q5 Hot Start High-Fidelity DNA Polymerase; long-product extension guidance for amplicons above routine PCR scale
representative.evidenceStatus: record-metadata-and-license-verified; representative is polymerase-specific and does not cover every long-amplicon length family
representative.selectionNote: Authoritative New England Biolabs record with stable DOI metadata, explicit Q5 polymerase identity, and a record PDF stating a Creative Commons Attribution License. Selected as the general high-fidelity long-PCR anchor; length and polymerase-family variants are retained as screened records and coverage gaps.

screened.title: A guide to long-range PCR for Nanopore sequencing
screened.reason: Useful 1-11 kb length and polymerase comparison, but specialized for cDNA/long-read Nanopore library preparation rather than general genomic long-range PCR.

screened.title: Long-range PCR
screened.reason: Specific Phusion-based 16.5 kb human mitochondrial amplification workflow with record-level Creative Commons evidence; narrower in organism, target, and polymerase than the selected general Q5 record.

coverageGaps: Polymerase-family variants beyond Q5, including Phusion and PrimeSTAR GXL, lack an independently qualified representative.

Sequencing-library and cDNA-specific long-range workflows are screened, but a general genomic-DNA representative for those length families is still missing.
nextSearchSuggestions: Search protocols.io and Bio-protocol for long-range PCR records explicitly using Phusion, PrimeSTAR GXL, or equivalent long-amplicon polymerases.
Search New England Biolabs for Q5 or LongAmp protocols with explicit 10-30 kb and ultra-long amplicon ranges.

representative.title: Bacterial and Yeast Colony PCR: how to get good results with a minimum of effort
representative.operation: Direct colony template PCR followed by agarose-gel amplicon sizing
representative.organism: Bacteria; Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Pichia, and Candida examples
representative.platform: Conventional thermocycler and agarose gel electrophoresis
representative.methodVariant: Colony PCR using premixed Taq systems with separate bacterial and yeast sample-preparation workflows; approximately 0.2-3 kb target range
representative.evidenceStatus: record-metadata-and-license-verified; representative covers colony screening but not tissue genotyping or allele-specific PCR
representative.selectionNote: Strong protocols.io record with stable DOI metadata, explicit bacterial and yeast colony sample variants, and a record PDF stating a Creative Commons Attribution License. Selected for the colony-screening branch because it directly separates sample preparation by organism while remaining reproducible-looking.

screened.title: E. coli Colony PCR
